notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with machine-readable codes: Reject invalid billing input by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly.errors, using short snake_case codes like "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity" and "negative_amount"; never raise bare ValueError in ledgerly modules.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0008] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per finance policy FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when the amount exceeds the threshold and no approver is given; amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary Decimal results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0002] Use to_money and ZERO from ledgerly.money: Normalize line prices with ledgerly.money.to_money and seed sums with ledgerly.money.ZERO, as line_total and invoice_total in ledgerly/invoice.py do.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0004] Guard mutations with invoice.status draft check: Before mutating an invoice, check invoice.status != "draft" and raise BillingError("invalid_state", f"invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}"), matching issue_invoice in ledgerly/invoice.py.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0005] Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`). Apply it to both the argument and `sub.started_at`.
  (learned from task E03 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
